name: mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp (Pi extension: list_mcp_tools + call_mcp)
pinned: 0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d (package.json 0.1.0, last commit 2026-02-22); deps from its package-lock: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.26.0, @mariozechner/pi-coding-agent 0.54.0, @mariozechner/jiti 2.6.5
engine: node:vm (vm.createContext + vm.Script.runInContext) inside the Pi host process; not a sandbox. The context is seeded with host-realm objects (Buffer, URL, setTimeout, console, the MCP bindings).
how_run: Loaded src/index.ts with jiti as Pi's extension loader does, passed a minimal ExtensionAPI, fired session_start, then called the registered call_mcp tool's execute({code, timeoutMs?}); the lookup tool is a local stdio MCP server (lookup-server.mjs) registered with --mcp-config mcp.json, HOME pointed at a probe-local folder so no user config or tokens are read.

P1.detail: printed 42, 1 host call. Tools are reached as call("host", "lookup", {id: 21}); the result is {content, structuredContent}, so the value is r.structuredContent.value.

P2.detail: All 200,000 printed chars came back in logs[0].message inside the JSON payload (200,144 chars total), no truncation, no marker. The literal bare-expression form returns no result field; `return "RETURNED"` returns result "RETURNED" plus the logs.

P3.detail: fetch is not a global (ReferenceError: fetch is not defined), but the host's fetch is one hop away: Buffer.constructor.constructor("return fetch")() fetched https://example.com and returned "200 577 bytes".

P4.detail: require -> ReferenceError; import("fs") -> TypeError ERR_VM_DYNAMIC_IMPORT_CALLBACK_MISSING; Deno -> ReferenceError. But Buffer.constructor.constructor("return process")().getBuiltinModule("fs").readFileSync("/etc/hosts") returned the file.

P5.detail: process.env.PROBE_SECRET -> ReferenceError: process is not defined; Buffer.constructor.constructor("return process")().env.PROBE_SECRET -> "s3cr3t".

P6.detail: node:vm runInContext timeout: "Script execution timed out after 30000ms" at 30,012 ms. Only the synchronous part is covered: `await null; while (true) {}` (P6b) runs on the host event loop after runInContext returns, the withTimeout timer can never fire, and the host process hung until the harness killed it at 120 s.
P6.display: limited (30 s; async loop hangs host)

P7.detail: No memory limit; code runs in the host process's V8 heap. The harness killed the host process at 4,106 MB process-tree RSS after 13.6 s. In Pi this is the agent's own process.

P8.detail: fresh globals: globalThis.kept printed gone (new vm context per call). The documented `state` object persists: the second call returned state.keptInState = 7.

P9.detail: parallel: 218 ms for 5 x 200 ms lookups, 5 host calls, all five arriving at the MCP server within 1 ms. The first run of a session includes about 400 ms of lazy server spawn (an early run measured 954 ms that way), so the harness warms the connection first. A direct MCP SDK client gave 209 ms as a control.

P10.detail: isError true; text is JSON {ok: false, error: {name: "Error", message: "probe-boom", stack}, logs}. The stack names call-mcp-user-script.js:4:9 (user line 1 + 3 wrapper lines; the multi-line case gives 6:7 for user line 3) and also leaks host frames with absolute paths (sandbox-runtime.ts:84, index.ts:356, the probe file).

P11.detail: median 3.8 ms, p90 8 ms in the first run under load average about 40; reruns 0.71 and 0.59 ms median, p90 0.83 to 1.16 ms. Each run is a new vm context in the host process. One-time setup (extension load, session_start, lazy MCP server spawn on first call) 335 to 694 ms.

P12.detail: this.constructor.constructor("return process")() -> "[object process]" (the context global was created in the host realm). Buffer.constructor.constructor("return process")().getBuiltinModule("child_process").execSync("echo PWNED") -> "PWNED\n". console.log.constructor.constructor reaches the same process (pid matches). call.constructor.constructor("return globalThis.__HOST_CANARY")() -> "host-canary". Only the sloppy-this form returned undefined.

hardened.config: call_mcp parameter timeoutMs: 1000 (the only limit the extension exposes; schema allows 100 to 300000, default 30000). https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/index.ts#L324-L330 and https://github.com/mitsuhiko/pi-codemode-mcp/blob/0ad55d6a8d6eeb44a255903bd10f22eacd72539d/src/sandbox-runtime.ts#L148-L157. 1000 ms rather than the 100 ms minimum so P9's 200 ms calls can finish. No memory, network or filesystem option exists.

P3.detail: Same as default: fetch not a global; the host fetch is reachable through any host-realm constructor (shown in default P3b).

P5.detail: PROBE_SECRET read as "s3cr3t" through the same escape.

P6.detail: "Script execution timed out after 1000ms" at 1,002 ms. The async variant `await null; while (true) {}` still hung the host until the 120 s kill (hardened-P6b.txt).
P6.display: limited (1 s; async loop hangs host)

P7.detail: Stopped by the 1 s vm timeout, not a memory limit, after host RSS reached 1,109 MB. The host survived; the next call returned "alive". A longer timeout or an allocation after an await would not be stopped.

P12.detail: Same five results as default, including execSync PWNED.

defaults.time: 30,000 ms (normalizeTimeout, sandbox-runtime.ts:148-157), applied as vm timeout min(timeoutMs, 60,000) to the synchronous part (sandbox-runtime.ts:83-88) and as a promise race (withTimeout, :159-179) that cannot fire while the host event loop is blocked.
defaults.memory: none; runs in the host process's V8 heap.
defaults.output: none in the extension; the whole {result, logs} payload is JSON-stringified (formatSandboxValue, sandbox-runtime.ts:102-114). Only the TUI renderer truncates lines for display (index.ts:414).
defaults.tool_calls: no cap. list_mcp_tools shows 20 tools inline (DEFAULT_INLINE_LIMIT, index.ts:33) and spills the rest to a temp .tsv.

source_notes.finding: README.md line 15: "The actual findings are that with how MCP works today, such efficiency gains are not useful." Lines 12-13 frame it: "This was an experiment to see if there is an efficiency benefit of allowing a coding agent interface with MCP in a way that allows composition." Lines 15-19 add that "an MCP server that uses code internally can be very helpful" and that mitsuhiko's google-workspace-mcp "actually performs as well as a similar skill does."

The engine is node:vm. vm.createContext is given host objects Buffer, URL, URLSearchParams, TextEncoder, TextDecoder, setTimeout, clearTimeout, a host console and __api with host async functions. Any of their .constructor.constructor is the host Function, which returns the host process (P12: execSync PWNED; P4/P5 read /etc/hosts and the env). The README calls it 'runs JavaScript in a sandbox'; node:vm is documented by Node as not a security mechanism.

The vm timeout covers only the synchronous run of the wrapping async IIFE. After the first await, user code runs as host microtasks; withTimeout's setTimeout cannot fire while a microtask spins, so `await null; while (true) {}` freezes the Pi process (P6b). No memory limit.

No generated per-tool functions. Code gets one generic call(server, tool, args), readResource(server, uri), listTools(query), plus servers, tools (server -> names) and resources maps. call() throws on MCP isError, adds schema hints, and retries once with snake_case -> camelCase args; it returns {content, structuredContent}.

On demand: list_mcp_tools(query) does case-insensitive text or /regex/ matching, shows 20 inline with compact signatures, and writes the full list to a temp .tsv for grep. In code, listTools(query) returns matches with inputSchema. Scales past 100 tools without putting schemas in the prompt.

Direct in-process function calls: the bindings are host async closures placed on __api, so a tool call is an ordinary host promise that goes to the MCP SDK Client (stdio/HTTP/SSE). Promise.all overlaps calls (P9 218 ms).
Returns JSON text {result, logs[]} where each log has level, message and ISO timestamp; errors return {ok: false, error: {name, message, stack}, logs}. No size cap.
New vm context per call (globals fresh), plus a documented `state` object owned by the runtime that persists across calls until resetState: true.

OAuth tokens are stored at ~/.pi/agent/mcp-oauth/<server>/tokens.json and bearer tokens in process env or memory, all host-side, but model code can reach them through the P12 escape (process.env, fs).

It is a Pi extension (package.json pi.extensions), not a standalone MCP server or proxy: it is an MCP client inside Pi. A regex rejects TypeScript-looking code before running it. The repo's own .mcp.json registers Sentry and GitHub Copilot MCP servers, so running Pi in the repo would contact them; the harness avoided that with --mcp-config and a probe cwd.

surprises: The README says call_mcp 'runs JavaScript in a sandbox'. It is node:vm seeded with host objects; P12 ran a shell command (execSync echo PWNED), P4 read /etc/hosts, P5 read the env secret, P3b reached example.com with the host fetch.
Even this.constructor.constructor("return process")(), the textbook first try, escapes, because the context global is a host-realm object.
The 30 s timeout does not cover code after the first await: `await null; while (true) {}` hangs the whole host process (P6b, default and hardened).
Error stacks leak absolute host paths of the extension and caller (P10).
It is not an MCP server/proxy but a Pi extension that is an MCP client; the README is the author's own negative result on code-mode efficiency over MCP.

The first call_mcp of a session pays a lazy MCP server spawn (about 400 ms), which made an unwarmed P9 look serial (954 ms) until the arrival timestamps showed all five calls reached the server within 1 ms.
